status: drafted grounded in the real Geneva 1560 extracted verse text (Assets/Resources/Verses/Geneva/ephesians_61.json), cross-checked against the existing KJV Ephesians Character Index for structural precedent only
notes: Read the full Geneva 1560 text of Ephesians (6 chapters, 155 verses: 23+22+21+32+33+24, matching the exact verse-per-chapter counts of the standard canonical Ephesians used in the existing KJV Character Index) before drafting anything. Verified this book has NO structural or content differences from the standard canon here - unlike some other books in this project (e.g. the Ethiopian "Ezra"), Geneva's Ephesians covers exactly the same pericopes in the same order as KJV's Ephesians: the same doctrinal arc in chapters 1-3 (election/redemption, Jew-Gentile reconciliation in one body, the mystery of Christ revealed to Paul) and the same practical arc in chapters 4-6 (unity of the Spirit and ministry gifts, put off the old man/put on the new, walking as children of light, the household code for wives/husbands/children/fathers/servants/masters, and the whole armour of God). Only two individuals are named anywhere in the letter, exactly as in KJV: Paul, who writes in the first person and repeatedly, personally identifies his own suffering ("I Paul am the prisoner of Iesus Christ for you Gentiles," 3:1; "I therefore, being prisoner in the Lord," 4:1; "ambassadour in bonds," 6:19-20) - a genuinely embodied author, so he keeps his own full person-tier - and Tychicus, named only as the courier who will personally deliver the letter and news (6:21-22), kept as a loyalty-boost submanager under Paul rather than his own tier or a law-tier deliveredBy, since his role is carrying the letter itself, not teaching its content. Every other party addressed - "the Saints, which are at Ephesus" (1:1), wives, husbands, children, fathers, servants, masters - is a generic class the text itself never individuates, so none are split into invented named characters, matching the rule against inventing differentiation the text doesn't support; they are folded into the relevant law/theme tier's purpose and verses instead. No naming collisions occur in this book. Real Geneva-specific translation-choice differences worth flagging (word-choice only, not content/canon differences - Geneva and KJV are both Protestant translations of the same underlying Greek text here): Geneva renders Ephesians 5:32 as "a great secrete" where KJV has "a great mystery" (the tier for that section is named after Geneva's own wording, 'the Great Secrete'); Geneva 2:14 reads "the stoppe of the partition wall" where KJV has "the middle wall of partition"; Geneva 6:4 reads fathers should raise children "in instruction and information of the Lord" where KJV has "nurture and admonition of the Lord" - a real, distinct word choice ("information" in its older sense of "forming/instructing," not the modern sense), included in the relevant tier's purpose text rather than silently normalized to KJV's phrasing. Every quoted verse note below is transcribed directly from the real Geneva 1560 text as extracted (archaic spelling preserved: "Iesus," "vs," "loue," "beleeue," "sonnes," etc.), not modernized or imported from KJV. All character/tier ids are suffixed "_geneva_ephesians" to avoid any collision with the existing KJV CharacterIndex ids for the same book/people.

scribeTiers.scribeName: Chosen Before the Foundation of the World
Wives, Husbands, and the Great Secrete

characters.name: Paul

verses.note: Opens the letter: "Pavl an Apostle of Jesvs Christ by the will of God, to the Saints, which are at Ephesus, and to ye faithfull in Christ Iesus."
Identifies himself: "I Paul am the prisoner of Iesus Christ for you Gentiles."
Made a minister "by the gift of the grace of God giuen vnto me," though "the least of all Saints," sent to preach among the Gentiles "the vnsearchable riches of Christ."
Desires "that ye faint not at my tribulations for your sakes, which is your glory."
Beseeches them, "I therefore, being prisoner in the Lord, praie you that yee walke worthie of the vocation whereunto yee are called."
Asks for prayer "that vtterance may be giuen vnto me, that I may open my mouth boldly to publish the secret of the Gospel, Whereof I am the ambassadour in bonds."
Sends Tychicus to the Ephesians "that ye might knowe mine affaires, and that he might comfort your hearts."

funFacts: Paul explicitly calls himself "prisoner" twice in the Geneva text of this letter (3:1, "the prisoner of Iesus Christ"; 4:1, "prisoner in the Lord") - the 6:20 line, "ambassadour in bonds," describes the same confinement with different wording, not a third repetition of the word "prisoner" itself.

No family or genealogical detail is given anywhere within Ephesians itself, so genealogy fields are left null rather than importing background from Acts or the other epistles, which lie outside this book's own text.

characters.name: Tychicus

verses.note: Paul calls him "my deare brother and faithfull minister in the Lord," who "shall shewe you of all things" concerning Paul's affairs.
Paul states he sent Tychicus "for the same purpose, that ye might knowe mine affaires, and that he might comfort your hearts."

funFacts: The only other individual named anywhere in this book, appearing solely as the personal courier who will deliver the letter and news of Paul - a supporting, faithful role, hence loyalty-boost rather than cost-cutter.

characters.name: Chosen Before the Foundation of the World
characters.scribeTier: Chosen Before the Foundation of the World
characters.purpose: Establishes the believer's standing as chosen by God's own grace before creation itself - predestinate to adoption through Iesus Christ, redeemed through his blood, and sealed with the holy Spirit of promise as "the earnest of our inheritance" - teaching that salvation's origin lies wholly in God's will and grace, not in human merit.

verses.note: "Blessed be God, and the Father of our Lord Iesus Christ, which hath blessed vs with all spirituall blessing in heauenly thinges in Christ."
"As hee hath chosen vs in him, before the foundation of the worlde, that we should be holy, and without blame before him in loue."
"Who hath predestinate vs, to be adopted through Iesus Christ in him selfe, according to the good pleasure of his will."
"By whom we haue redemption through his blood, euen the forgiuenes of sinnes, according to his rich grace."

Believers, "after that ye beleeued, ye were sealed with the holy Spirite of promise, Which is the earnest of our inheritance, for the redemption of that libertie purchased vnto the prayse of his glory."

characters.name: The Eyes of Your Understanding
characters.purpose: Paul's prayer that the Saints receive "the Spirit of wisedome, and reuelation" so the eyes of their understanding might be lightened to know the hope of their calling and the riches of Christ's glorious inheritance - grounded in the "exceeding greatnesse of his power," the same power that raised Christ from the dead and set him as head over the Church, "which is his body."

verses.note: Prays God would giue them "the Spirit of wisedome, and reuelation through the acknowledging of him."
"That the eyes of your vnderstanding may be lightened, that ye may knowe what the hope is of his calling."
The "exceeding greatnesse of his power toward vs" is the same power "he wrought in Christ, when he raised him from the dead."
God "hath giuen him ouer all things to be the head to the Church, Which is his body, euen the fulnesse of him that filleth all in all things."

characters.name: Quickened Together in Christ
characters.purpose: Describes salvation as God's rescue of the spiritually dead - "by grace are ye saued through faith... not of workes, least any man should boast himselfe" - teaching that believers are God's own "workemanship created in Christ Iesus vnto good workes," so good works are grace's fruit, never its cause.

verses.note: The Ephesians were formerly "dead in trespasses and sinnes."
"God which is rich in mercie, through his great loue wherewith he loued vs... hath quickened vs together in Christ, by whose grace ye are saued."
"For by grace are ye saued through faith, and that not of your selues: it is the gift of God, Not of workes, least any man should boast himselfe."
"We are his workemanship created in Christ Iesus vnto good workes, which God hath ordeined, that we should walke in them."

characters.name: One New Man of Twain
characters.purpose: Explains the reconciliation of Jew and Gentile in Christ - "the stoppe of the partition wall" broken down, both made "one newe man," and built together as "an holy Temple in the Lord," with Christ himself the "chiefe corner stone" - teaching that peace between former strangers comes specifically through the cross, not mere goodwill.

verses.note: "He is our peace, which hath made of both one, and hath broken the stoppe of the partition wall."
Christ's purpose: "for to make of twaine one newe man in himselfe, so making peace."
Christ's purpose: "that he might reconcile both vnto God in one body by his crosse, and slay hatred thereby."
Christ "came, and preached peace to you which were afarre off, and to them that were neere. For through him we both haue an entrance vnto the Father by one Spirit."
Gentile believers are now "citizens with the Saintes, and of the houshold of God... built vpon the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets, Iesus Christ himselfe being the chiefe corner stone."
The whole building "groweth vnto an holy Temple in the Lord," believers "built together to be the habitation of God by the Spirit."

characters.name: The Mystery Now Revealed
characters.purpose: Explains the "mysterie of Christ" specifically shewed to Paul by revelation - that the Gentiles are "inheriters also, and of the same body, and partakers of his promise in Christ by the Gospel" - grounding Paul's own calling as apostle to the Gentiles in this revealed mystery, not personal ambition.

verses.note: The mystery was shewed him "by reuelation (as I wrote aboue in fewe wordes, Whereby when ye reade, ye may knowe mine vnderstanding in the mysterie of Christ)."
The mystery "Which in other ages was not opened vnto the sonnes of men, as it is nowe reueiled vnto his holy Apostles and Prophets by the Spirit."
"That the Gentiles should be inheriters also, and of the same body, and partakers of his promise in Christ by the Gospel."
"Euen vnto me the least of all Saints is this grace giuen, that I should preach among the Gentiles the vnsearchable riches of Christ."
Purpose: to make cleare "what the fellowship of the mysterie is" so "the manifolde wisedome of God" is knowen by the Church even to "principalities and powers in heauenly places."

characters.name: Rooted and Grounded in Love
characters.purpose: Paul's prayer that Christ dwell in the saints' hearts by faith, that they be "rooted and grounded in loue" and able to comprehend the vastness of Christ's love "which passeth knowledge" - closing in a doxology to the God "able to do exceeding aboundantly aboue all that we aske or thinke."

verses.note: Prays they be "strengthened by his Spirit in the inner man, That Christ may dwell in your heartes by faith."
Prays they, "being rooted and grounded in loue," comprehend "the breadth, and length, and depth, and height: And to knowe the loue of Christ, which passeth knowledge."
Closing doxology: "Vnto him therefore that is able to do exceeding aboundantly aboue all that we aske or thinke... Be praise in the Church by Christ Iesus, throughout all generations for euer, Amen."

characters.name: The Unity of the Spirit
characters.purpose: Calls believers to walke worthy of their calling in humbleness and unity - "one body, and one Spirit... one Lord, one Faith, one Baptisme, One God and Father of all" - grounds that unity in grace given "according to the measure of the gift of Christ," and explains that Christ gaue apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors and teachers to repair the Saints and build up the body "till we all meete together... vnto a perfite man."

verses.note: Calls for "all humblenesse of minde, and meekenesse, with long suffering, supporting one an other through loue, Endeuouring to keepe the vnitie of the Spirit in the bond of peace."
"There is one body, and one Spirit... There is one Lord, one Faith, one Baptisme, One God and Father of all."
"Vnto euery one of vs is giuen grace, according to the measure of the gift of Christ."

Quoting the Psalm, "Whe he asceded vp on hie, he led captiuity captiue, and gaue gifts vnto men" - he that "descended first into the lowest partes of the earth" is the same "that ascended, farre aboue all heauens, that hee might fill all things."
Christ "gaue some to be Apostles, and some Prophets, and some Euangelists, and some Pastours, and Teachers, For the repairing of the Saintes, for the woorke of the ministerie."
"Folowe the truth in loue, and in all things, grow vp into him, which is the head, that is, Christ."

characters.name: Put Off the Old Man
characters.purpose: A direct call to abandon the former "vanitie" of Gentile living, be "renued in the spirit of your minde," and "put on ye new man, which after God is created vnto righteousnes, and true holines" - worked out in concrete instruction against lying, unresolved anger, theft, and corrupt speech, with a warning not to "grieue the holy Spirit of God."

verses.note: Testifies "that yee hencefoorth walke not as other Gentiles walke, in vanitie of their minde" - past feeling, giuen to wantonness and vncleannesse.
Instructs them to cast off "that olde man, which is corrupt through the deceiueable lustes" and "put on ye new man, which after God is created vnto righteousnes, and true holines."
"Cast off lying, and speake euery man truth vnto his neighbour: for we are members one of another."
"Bee angrie, but sinne not: let not the sunne goe downe vpon your wrath."
"Let him that stole, steale no more: but let him rather labour, and worke with his handes the thing which is good."
"Grieue not the holy Spirit of God, by whom ye are sealed vnto ye day of redemption."
Calls to put away "all bitternesse, and anger, and wrath, crying, and euill speaking" and instead "be ye courteous one to another, and tender hearted, freely forgiuing one another."

characters.name: Walk as Children of Light
characters.purpose: Exhorts believers to "bee yee therefore followers of God, as deare children" and "walke in loue," to have no fellowship with "ye vnfruitfull works of darknes," and to be "fulfilled with the Spirit" rather than drunk with wine - that fullness expressed through singing psalms and hymns and giving thanks, summed up as "submitting your selues one to another in the feare of God."

verses.note: "Bee yee therefore followers of God, as deare children, And walke in loue, euen as Christ hath loued vs."
"Ye were once darkenesse, but are nowe light in the Lord: walke as children of light."
"Haue no fellowship with ye vnfruitfull works of darknes, but euen reproue them rather."
"Be not drunke with wine, wherein is excesse: but be fulfilled with the Spirit, Speaking vnto your selues in psalmes, and hymnes, and spirituall songs."
"Submitting your selues one to another in the feare of God."

characters.name: Wives, Husbands, and the Great Secrete
characters.scribeTier: Wives, Husbands, and the Great Secrete
characters.purpose: Sets out the household code for marriage - wives submitting themselves to their husbands "as vnto the Lord," husbands loving their wives "euen as Christ loued the Church, and gaue himselfe for it" - explicitly framed as a living picture of Christ and the Church: "this is a great secrete."

verses.note: "Wiues, submit your selues vnto your husbands, as vnto the Lord. For the husband is the wiues head, euen as Christ is the head of the Church."
"Husbands, loue your wiues, euen as Christ loued the Church, and gaue himselfe for it."
Husbands "ought to loue their wiues, as their owne bodies... euen as the Lord doeth the Church."
"They twaine shalbe one flesh. This is a great secrete, but I speake concerning Christ, and concerning the Church."

characters.name: Children, Fathers, Servants, and Masters
characters.purpose: Extends the household code to parent-child and master-servant relationships - children obeying parents "in the Lord" under "the first commandement with promise," fathers not provoking children to wrath but bringing them up "in instruction and information of the Lord," servants serving "as vnto Christ" with singleness of heart, and masters doing the same toward servants, "knowe that euen your master also is in heauen, neither is there respect of person with him."

verses.note: "Children, obey your parents in the Lord... Honour thy father and mother (which is the first commandement with promise)."
"Ye, fathers, prouoke not your children to wrath: but bring them vp in instruction and information of the Lord."
"Seruants, be obedient vnto them that are your masters... as the seruants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart."
"Ye masters, doe the same things vnto them, putting away threatning: and know that euen your master also is in heauen, neither is there respect of person with him."

characters.name: The Whole Armour of God
characters.purpose: A vivid closing exhortation to spiritual warfare - the Christian's struggle is "not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, and against the worldly gouernours, the princes of the darkenesse of this worlde, against spirituall wickednesses, which are in ye hie places" - met by taking up each piece of "the whole armour of God" (verity, righteousness, the Gospel of peace, faith, salvation, and "the sword of the Spirit, which is the worde of God"), sustained by watchful prayer.

verses.note: "Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the assaultes of the deuil. For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, and against the worldly gouernours, the princes of the darkenesse of this worlde."
"Stand therefore, and your loynes girded about with veritie, and hauing on the brest plate of righteousnesse."
"Your feete shod with the preparation of the Gospel of peace... take the shielde of faith, wherewith ye may quench all the fierie dartes of the wicked."
"Take the helmet of saluation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the worde of God."
"Pray alwayes with all maner prayer and supplication in the Spirit: and watch thereunto with all perseuerance and supplication for al Saints."

genealogyLists.note: Geneva's Ephesians names almost no individuals at all, matching the standard canon exactly - the addressees are a collective, "the Saints, which are at Ephesus, and to ye faithfull in Christ Iesus" (1:1), and the household-code categories (wives, husbands, children, fathers, servants, masters) are addressed as generic classes throughout chapters 5-6, never individuated by the text. Nothing here is invented as a separate named character, per the rule against inventing differentiation the text doesn't support. Paul's own broader biography (Acts, the other epistles) is deliberately not imported - it lies outside Ephesians' own text and this book's indexed scope.

the_saints_at_ephesus.note: The letter's collective addressees - "the Saints, which are at Ephesus, and to ye faithfull in Christ Iesus" - never individually named.

closing_benediction.note: Paul's closing blessing of "Peace... and loue with faith from God the Father, and from the Lord Iesus Christ" and "Grace... with all them which loue our Lord Iesus Christ, to their immortalitie" - addressed to the same collective body, not a person.
